faq.title: Questions foreign companies ask us
faq.note: Information on this page is general and is not legal advice.

items.q: Can you register a branch or representative office of a foreign company in Iraq?
items.a: Yes. We register foreign branches and representative offices, prepare and follow up the legal incorporation documents, and complete the registration procedures before the relevant authorities.

items.q: What are the main steps for a foreign company?
items.a: Our foreign-company track has four steps: register the branch (prepare, legalise and file the branch documents); open the company's tax and social security files; arrange residency and work permits for foreign staff; and stay compliant with contracts, labour matters, renewals and filings.

items.q: Can you handle work permits and residency for our foreign employees?
items.a: Yes. We process work visa and residency procedures, obtain work permits and authorizations for foreign employees, and provide administrative support for expatriate staff and executives.

items.q: Do you advise on Iraqi tax and social security?
items.a: Yes. We provide legal consultations on Iraqi tax regulations, monitor companies' tax obligations, represent companies in tax disputes, and handle social security and employment insurance matters.

items.q: Can we work with you in English?
items.a: Yes. Advice, documents and correspondence are available in both Arabic and English.

items.q: How are scope and fees agreed?
items.a: Scope, timeline and fees are agreed in writing before work begins. Each engagement starts with a consultation and a review of your documents, followed by a written proposal.
